subject: math
title: The Cartesian Plane: Four Quadrants, Translations, Reflections and Rotations
seo_title: Grade 6 Cartesian Plane and Transformations Worksheets: Four Quadrants (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants of a Cartesian plane, and describe the translations that move a point from one coordinate to another; describe and perform combinations of translations, reflections, and rotations up to 360° on a grid, and predict the results
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on the Cartesian plane for the Ontario curriculum: plot points in all four quadrants, name quadrants from the signs, translate points, reflect them in the axes and rotate them 90° and 180° about the origin. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: In (x, y), x tells you left or right and y tells you up or down. A minus sign means left or down.
key_sub: Quadrants I to IV go counterclockwise from the top right. A translation changes x (left or right) or y (up or down). A reflection in the x-axis changes the sign of y; in the y-axis, the sign of x. A 180° rotation about the origin changes both signs.
body_html:
The four quadrants

On the Cartesian plane, the x-axis and the y-axis are number lines that include negative numbers. They cross at the origin, (0, 0), and cut the plane into four quadrants. The quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

In (x, y), x always comes first. The sign tells the direction. Positive x: right. Negative x: left. Positive y: up. Negative y: down.

QuadrantWhereSigns (x, y)Example
Itop right(+, +)(2, 5)
IItop left(−, +)(−3, 4)
IIIbottom left(−, −)(−6, −1)
IVbottom right(+, −)(4, −2)

A point on an axis, like (0, −4) or (5, 0), is not in any quadrant.

Example

Which quadrant is (−2, −5) in?

x is negative (left) and y is negative (down). Left and down is the bottom left.

Answer: Quadrant III

Translations: sliding a point

A move left or right changes only x. A move up or down changes only y.

MoveWhat happensExample from (2, 1)
3 units rightx + 3(5, 1)
3 units leftx − 3(−1, 1)
3 units upy + 3(2, 4)
3 units downy − 3(2, −2)
Example

Describe the translation from (−3, 2) to (2, 2).

Only x changes. From −3 to the y-axis is 3 spaces, then 2 more: 3 + 2 = 5.

Answer: 5 units right

Reflections in the axes

An axis works like a mirror. Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of y. Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of x.

Example

Reflect (−4, 5) in the x-axis.

The x-axis is the mirror, so the point flips down. x stays −4. y changes sign: 5 → −5.

Answer: (−4, −5)

Rotations about the origin

A rotation turns a point around the origin. It stays the same distance from the origin. Say how far (90°, 180°, 270° or 360°) and which way (clockwise or counterclockwise).

To rotate, describe the point from the origin, then turn each direction. A quarter turn (90°) clockwise turns right into down and up into right. A half turn (180°) turns right into left and up into down, so both signs change. A full turn (360°) brings the point back where it started.

Rotation about the originPatternExample from (4, 2)
90° clockwise(x, y) → (y, opposite of x)(2, −4)
90° counterclockwise(x, y) → (opposite of y, x)(−2, 4)
180°both signs change(−4, −2)
360°no change(4, 2)
Example

Rotate (−3, 5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

(−3, 5) is 3 left and 5 up. A quarter turn counterclockwise turns left into down and up into left. So the image is 5 left and 3 down.

Answer: (−5, −3)

Combination

Reflect (1, 4) in the x-axis, then reflect the image in the y-axis.

(1, 4) → (1, −4) → (−1, −4). Both signs changed, so the two reflections give the same result as a 180° rotation.

Answer: (−1, −4)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the numbers: plotting (−3, 4) at (4, −3)Move across first (x), then up or down (y)
Dropping the minus signNegative x means left; negative y means down
Numbering the quadrants clockwiseGo counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right
Counting grid lines instead of spacesCount the jumps between lines; the starting line is 0
From −3 to 2 doing 3 − 2 = 1The move crosses an axis, so add: 3 + 2 = 5
Reflecting in the wrong axisIn the x-axis, y changes sign. In the y-axis, x changes sign
Rotating the wrong wayClockwise goes the way clock hands move: from the top to the right
Only swapping the numbers in a 90° turn: (4, 2) → (2, 4)Swap and change one sign: (2, −4) clockwise, (−2, 4) counterclockwise

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about the Cartesian plane in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 6 (Spatial Sense, E1), students plot and read points in all four quadrants, describe translations from one point to another, and perform and predict combinations of translations, reflections and rotations up to 360°.

faq.q: How are the four quadrants numbered?
faq.a: Counterclockwise from the top right: Quadrant I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −) and IV (+, −). A point on an axis, like (0, −4), is not in any quadrant.

faq.q: How do you rotate a point 90° about the origin?
faq.a: Describe the point from the origin, then turn each direction. For 90° clockwise, right becomes down and up becomes right, so (4, 2) goes to (2, −4); a 180° turn changes both signs.

faq.q: Is the Cartesian plane on the Grade 6 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, which includes the spatial sense expectations on coordinates and transformations. Practising these questions helps students get ready for it.

sets.title: Read and plot points in all four quadrants

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then up 4. Point A is at (−3, 4). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 5, then down 2. Point B is at (5, −2). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then down 5. Point C is at (−4, −5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (−5, −4) is point D: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 2, then down 6. Point E is at (2, −6). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 3, then down 5. Point G is at (3, −5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (−5, 3) is point H: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 6, then up 2. Point K is at (−6, 2). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 4. Point M is at (0, −4). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point R?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then 0 up or down. Point R is at (−5, 0). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point P?
items.e: Point P is 4 units to the left of the origin, so x = −4. Left means negative. (2 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point Q?
items.e: Point Q is 6 units below the x-axis, so y = −6. Down means negative. (3 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: Which point is at (−3, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then up 4: that is point D. Point A is at (4, −3): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (2, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 2, then down 5: that is point B. Point A is at (−5, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−4, −2)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then down 2: that is point C. Point A is at (−2, −4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−5, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then up 3: that is point A. Point B is at (3, −5): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (0, −3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 3: that is point A. Point B is at (−3, 0): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−2, 5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then up 5: that is point D. Point A is at (5, −2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: To plot (−5, 2), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, −5, is the x-coordinate. It is negative, so go left 5. Then go up 2.

items.q: A point is 3 units left of the origin and 4 units up. Amira writes its coordinates as (4, −3). What mistake did she make?
c: She counted the grid lines, not the spaces
items.e: The point is (−3, 4): left 3 gives x = −3, up 4 gives y = 4. Amira put the numbers in the wrong order. Always write x (across) first.

items.q: Aiden starts at the origin. He goes left 4, then down 3. Which coordinates name his point?
items.e: Left 4 gives x = −4. Down 3 gives y = −3. Write x first: (−4, −3).

items.q: A point is 6 units to the right of the y-axis and 2 units below the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
items.e: Right of the y-axis means x is positive: x = 6. Below the x-axis means y is negative: y = −2. The point is (6, −2).

sets.title: Quadrants and the signs of coordinates

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−2, −5) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−2, −5) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (4, −6) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (4, −6) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−3, 6) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−3, 6) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (6, 1) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (6, 1) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−6, −1) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−6, −1) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (1, −4) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (1, −4) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−5, 2) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−5, 2) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (5, 5) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (5, 5) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Where is the point (0, −4)?
items.e: x = 0, so the point does not move left or right. It goes down 4 along the y-axis. A point on an axis is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (−6, 0)?
items.e: y = 0, so the point does not move up or down. It goes left 6 along the x-axis. It is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 0)?
items.e: (0, 0) is the origin, where the two axes cross. It is on both axes and in no quadrant.

items.q: In which quadrant are both coordinates negative?
items.e: Negative x means left and negative y means down. Left and down is the bottom-left part: Quadrant III.

items.q: A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
items.e: Positive x means right and negative y means down. Right and down is the bottom-right part: Quadrant IV.

items.q: What are the signs of the coordinates of a point in Quadrant II?
items.e: Quadrant II is the top-left part. Left means x is negative and up means y is positive: (−, +).

items.q: Which point could be in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Quadrant IV is the bottom-right part: x positive (right), y negative (down). (4, −2) is right 4 and down 2.

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant II?
items.e: Quadrant II is the top-left part: x negative, y positive. (−5, 6) is left 5 and up 6. ((5, −6) is in Quadrant IV: that is where Quadrant II would be if you counted clockwise.)

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant III?
items.e: Point A is at (−3, −4). x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−3, −4) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Point B is at (5, −3). x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (5, −3) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right. Point A is in Quadrant II: counting clockwise by mistake would call it IV.

items.q: Owen says (−3, 5) is in Quadrant IV. What mistake did he make?
items.e: (−3, 5) is left and up: Quadrant II. The quadrants go counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right.

items.q: Hana says (0, −4) is in Quadrant IV. Is she right?
c: No, it is on the x-axis
No, it is in Quadrant III
No, it is on the y-axis, not in a quadrant
items.e: x = 0, so the point sits on the y-axis, 4 units below the origin. Points on an axis are not in any quadrant.

items.q: Point (−2, 3) is translated 3 units left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only x changes. x: 3 left from −2 is −5. The new point is (−5, 3).

items.q: Point (4, −1) is translated 4 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only y changes. y: 4 down from −1 is −5. The new point is (4, −5).

items.q: Point (−5, −2) is translated 6 units right. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only x changes. x: 6 right from −5 is 1. The new point is (1, −2).

items.q: Point (3, 4) is translated 6 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only y changes. y: 6 down from 4 is −2. The new point is (3, −2).

items.q: Point (−1, −4) is translated 5 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only y changes. y: 5 up from −4 is 1. The new point is (−1, 1).

items.q: Point (2, 5) is translated 6 units left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Only x changes. x: 6 left from 2 is −4. The new point is (−4, 5).

items.q: Point (−3, 2) is translated 5 units right and 4 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x: 5 right from −3 is 2, then y: 4 down from 2 is −2. The new point is (2, −2).

items.q: Point (4, −1) is translated 6 units left and 3 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x: 6 left from 4 is −2, then y: 3 up from −1 is 2. The new point is (−2, 2).

items.q: A point moves from (−3, 2) to (2, 2). Describe the translation.
items.e: Only x changes, from −3 to 2. Count the spaces: 3 to the y-axis, then 2 more, so 3 + 2 = 5 units right. (6 comes from counting the grid lines.)

items.q: A point moves from (4, −3) to (4, 3). Describe the translation.
items.e: Only y changes, from −3 to 3. That is 3 up to the x-axis and 3 more: 3 + 3 = 6 units up.

items.q: A point moves from (1, 4) to (−4, 1). Describe the translation.
items.e: x goes from 1 to −4: 1 to the y-axis and 4 more, so 5 units left. y goes from 4 to 1: 3 units down.

items.q: A point moves from (−5, −3) to (2, 1). Describe the translation.
items.e: x goes from −5 to 2: 5 + 2 = 7 units right. y goes from −3 to 1: 3 + 1 = 4 units up. The moves cross an axis, so add; do not subtract 5 − 2.

items.q: Point (x, y) is translated 3 units left. Which shows its new coordinates?
items.e: Left and right moves change only x. Left makes x smaller, so subtract 3: (x − 3, y). y stays the same.

items.q: A point moves from (x, y) to (x, y − 2). How did it move?
items.e: Only y changed, so the point moved up or down. y got 2 smaller, so the point moved 2 units down.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units right and 2 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: P is at (−4, 4). x: 6 right from −4 is 2, then y: 2 down from 4 is 2. The image is (2, 2): point D. Point C comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units left and 3 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: P is at (3, 1). x: 6 left from 3 is −3, then y: 3 down from 1 is −2. The image is (−3, −2): point A. Point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 4 units right and 3 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: P is at (−3, −1). x: 4 right from −3 is 1, then y: 3 up from −1 is 2. The image is (1, 2): point C. Point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Describe the translation from P to Q.
items.e: P is at (−5, 3) and Q is at (2, −2). x: −5 to 2 is 5 + 2 = 7 units right. y: 3 to −2 is 3 + 2 = 5 units down. Both moves cross an axis, so add. Count the spaces between the lines, not the lines.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A (−4, 1), B (−1, 1) and C (−1, 4). It is translated 5 units right and 6 units down. Where does C land?
items.e: Every vertex moves the same way. C is at (−1, 4). x: 5 right from −1 is 4. y: 6 down from 4 is −2 (4 down to the x-axis, then 2 more). C lands on (4, −2).

items.q: In a board game, Emma’s counter is on (−2, −3). She moves it 6 units right and 5 units up. Where is it now?
items.e: x: 6 right from −2 is 4 (2 to the y-axis, then 4 more). y: 5 up from −3 is 2 (3 to the x-axis, then 2 more). The counter is on (4, 2).

sets.title: Reflections in the x-axis and y-axis

items.q: Reflect (3, −2) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −2 and x changes sign, 3 → −3. The image is (−3, −2).

items.q: Reflect (−4, 5) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −4 and y changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−4, −5).

items.q: Reflect (6, 1) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays 1 and x changes sign, 6 → −6. The image is (−6, 1).

items.q: Reflect (−2, −6) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −6 → 6. The image is (−2, 6).

items.q: Reflect (5, 4) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays 5 and y changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is (5, −4).

items.q: Reflect (−6, −3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −3 and x changes sign, −6 → 6. The image is (6, −3).

items.q: Reflect (0, 6) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, 6) is on the y-axis, the mirror line itself, so its reflection is the same point: (0, 6).

items.q: Reflect (−5, 0) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−5, 0) is on the x-axis, the mirror line itself, so its reflection is the same point: (−5, 0).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−3, 2). In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −3 and y changes sign, 2 → −2. The image is (−3, −2). That is point D. Point A is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (4, −3). In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −3 and x changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is (−4, −3). That is point C. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−2, −4). In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −4 → 4. The image is (−2, 4). That is point A. Point B is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, 2). In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays 2 and x changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−5, 2). That is point B. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: The points (4, 1) and (−4, 1) are reflections of each other in which axis?
items.e: Only the x-coordinate changes sign (4 → −4), so the points flip left and right. The mirror line is the y-axis.

items.q: The points (−3, 5) and (−3, −5) are reflections of each other in which axis?
items.e: Only the y-coordinate changes sign (5 → −5), so the points flip up and down. The mirror line is the x-axis.

items.q: (2, −6) is reflected in one axis and then in the other. Where does it land?
items.e: In the x-axis: (2, −6) → (2, 6). Then in the y-axis: (2, 6) → (−2, 6). Both signs change.

items.q: Are (3, 4) and (4, 3) reflections of each other in an axis?
items.e: A reflection in an axis keeps the same numbers and changes one sign. Here the numbers are swapped, and no sign changes.

items.q: When you reflect a point in the x-axis, what changes?
items.e: The x-axis is a mirror lying flat. The point flips up or down, so only y changes sign. Example: (2, 3) → (2, −3).

items.q: Point Q is the reflection of point P in the y-axis. Q is at (−3, 4). Where is P?
items.e: Reflecting in the y-axis changes only the sign of x, and reflecting back does the same. (−3, 4) → (3, 4).

items.q: Point (−6, 2) is reflected in the y-axis. Which quadrant is the image in?
items.e: The image is (6, 2). Both coordinates are positive, so it is in Quadrant I.

items.q: Lucas reflects (2, 5) in the x-axis and gets (−2, 5). What mistake did he make?
items.e: He changed the sign of x, which is a reflection in the y-axis. In the x-axis, y changes sign: (2, −5).

sets.title: Rotations about the origin and combinations of moves

items.q: Rotate (3, 1) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (3, 1) is 3 right and 1 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 1 right and 3 down from the origin: (1, −3).

items.q: Rotate (−2, 4) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−2, 4) is 2 left and 4 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 4 right and 2 up from the origin: (4, 2).

items.q: Rotate (−5, −3) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−5, −3) is 5 left and 3 down from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 3 left and 5 up from the origin: (−3, 5).

items.q: Rotate (4, 2) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (4, 2) is 4 right and 2 up from the origin. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 2 left and 4 up from the origin: (−2, 4).

items.q: Rotate (−1, 5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−1, 5) is 1 left and 5 up from the origin. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 5 left and 1 down from the origin: (−5, −1).

items.q: Rotate (6, −3) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (6, −3) is 6 right and 3 down from the origin. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 3 right and 6 up from the origin: (3, 6).

items.q: Rotate (2, −5) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (2, −5) is 2 right and 5 down from the origin. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So the image is 2 left and 5 up from the origin: (−2, 5).

items.q: Rotate (−4, 3) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−4, 3) is 4 left and 3 up from the origin. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So the image is 4 right and 3 down from the origin: (4, −3).

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P (4, 1) is 4 right and 1 up from the origin. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 1 left and 4 up from the origin: (−1, 4). That is point C. Point A is a 90° clockwise turn: the wrong way.

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P (−3, 2) is 3 left and 2 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 2 right and 3 up from the origin: (2, 3). That is point D. Point A is a 90° counterclockwise turn: the wrong way.

items.q: Point P is rotated 180° about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P (−5, −2) is 5 left and 2 down from the origin. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So the image is 5 right and 2 up from the origin: (5, 2). That is point B. Points A and C are reflections in one axis, where only one sign changes.

items.q: Point (−4, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Which quadrant is the image in?
items.e: (−4, 3) is in Quadrant II. A quarter turn clockwise moves it to the next quadrant clockwise: from the top left to the top right. The image is (3, 4), in Quadrant I.

items.q: Point (2, 5) is rotated about the origin and lands on (−5, 2). Describe the rotation.
items.e: (2, 5) is 2 right and 5 up. (−5, 2) is 5 left and 2 up. Right turned into up and up turned into left: that is a quarter turn counterclockwise. (90° clockwise would give (5, −2).)

items.q: Point (2, 5) is rotated 270° counterclockwise about the origin. Where does it land?
items.e: 270° counterclockwise is 3 quarter turns counterclockwise. That ends in the same place as 1 quarter turn clockwise (360° − 270° = 90°). (2, 5) is 2 right and 5 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 5 right and 2 down from the origin: (5, −2).

items.q: Liam rotates (4, 1) 90° clockwise about the origin and gets (−1, 4). What mistake did he make?
c: He swapped the numbers and changed no sign
items.e: (−1, 4) is a quarter turn counterclockwise. (4, 1) is 4 right and 1 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 1 right and 4 down from the origin: (1, −4). Check: (4, 1) is in Quadrant I, and a clockwise turn takes it to Quadrant IV.

items.q: Nathan makes a snowflake design for the class window. One tip is at (−3, 5). He rotates the design 360° about the origin. Where is that tip now?
items.e: 360° is a full turn, so every point comes back to where it started. The tip is still at (−3, 5).

items.q: Priya draws a point at (1, 4) for a quilt pattern. She reflects it in the x-axis, then reflects the image in the y-axis. Which single move gives the same result?
items.e: In the x-axis: (1, 4) → (1, −4). Then in the y-axis: (1, −4) → (−1, −4). Both signs changed, and that is what a 180° rotation about the origin does.

items.q: In a video game, Ava’s spaceship is at (−2, 6). The screen is a grid with the origin in the centre. The ship is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Where is it now?
items.e: (−2, 6) is 2 left and 6 up from the origin. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 6 right and 2 up from the origin: (6, 2).

items.q: In a coding app, Benjamin’s sprite is at (−4, −3). He translates it 6 units right, then rotates it 180° about the origin. Where does it end up?
items.e: Do the moves in order. 6 right from (−4, −3): x goes from −4 to 2, so the sprite is at (2, −3). A 180° rotation changes both signs: (2, −3) → (−2, 3).

items.q: Leah designs a pinwheel for a Terry Fox Run poster. One blade tip is at (1, 5). The next blade is the first one rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Where is the next tip?
items.e: (1, 5) is 1 right and 5 up from the origin. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 5 left and 1 up from the origin: (−5, 1).
